quotes.text: "classic signature keeps base64 for a clean body"

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The cleanup regression restored transfer encoding for signed-only PGP/MIME so message transport rewrites cannot invalidate a detached signature. Current code also forces encoding when GPGME signs, including encrypted mail, because that backend can transform UTF-8 bytes. Inline signing remains separate. Newer MimeMessage permits a clean body to remain 7bit for the unobtrusive signature format even when forceMsgEncoding is set; classic multipart signatures retain base64 in the focused test, while non-ASCII, controls and long lines remain encoded. Do not teach a blanket always-base64 rule or infer that a comment about wrapping replaces the current condition. No send transition or cryptographic validation was run.
title: PGP transfer encoding has signature and backend-specific exceptions
